newsitem.title: FRANCE: MOTOR RACING-PROST BACK AS TEAM BOSS.
newsitem.headline: MOTOR RACING-PROST BACK AS TEAM BOSS.

text.p: Four times world champion Alain Prost has reached an agreement to take over Ligier and will run his own Formula One team in this year's world championship.
French manufacturer Peugeot, whose engines will be fitted in Prost's cars from next year, said on Thursday that the deal would be made official at a news conference on Friday in Paris.

Ligier refused to comment on a report in the sports daily L'Equipe which said Ligier would become Prost Grand Prix and contest the 1997 series with drivers Olivier Panis of France and Shinji Nakano of Japan.
Prost will rely on the new Ligier JS 45 cars powered by a Mugen-Honda engine this season.
But from 1998 and for three years, his cars will be fitted with the Peugeot V10 engines currently used by the Jordan team, a Peugeot spokesman said.
Prost needed the agreement of all the existing teams to change the Ligier name but he had to wait until Wednesday to gain Jordan boss Eddie Jordan's signature, said L'Equipe.

Jordan was afraid he might lose his supply of Peugeot engines but was reassured when he learned that the deal reached by Prost would allow him to continue with Peugeot in 1997, a source close to Peugeot said.

At the unveiling of his new car last month, Jordan played down the rumours about any threat to his team but admitted that 1997 would be the final year of his own three-year deal with the French manufacturer.

The Ligier team were created in 1976 and scored eight grand prix wins from 1977 to 1981. In 1994 the struggling outfit was bought by Italian Flavio Briatore who wanted to obtain their Renault engine for his own Benetton cars.

Despite losing the Renault engine, Ligier improved consistently under Briatore's rule and last year Panis drove the team to a stunning victory in Monaco. They finished sixth in the constructors' world championship with 15 points.
"A lot of progress has been made," said Briatore at the launching of the new Ligier last month. "Ligier are still a top team and can still improve."
Briatore admitted then he was in favour of selling Ligier to the Frenchman in order to concentrate his efforts on Benetton.
Prost scored a record 51 grand prix wins in his career which ended in 1993 with his fourth world championship title.
